GH_and_fault_scope.interpretation: The published sum-of-all-omitted-access <=0.5 mOhm and complete connected subgraphs is a sufficient lifting certificate, not necessary physical feasibility. It is not implied by a 0.1 mOhm selected path target. Expanded actual graph or compatible field bounds can avoid that overstrong surrogate while retaining GH<=0.5 A and original voltage/current requirements.
GH_and_fault_scope.upstream: Preserve external load-side boundary and existing fault obligations; no upstream protection design undertaken or required as the next deliverable of this source-only candidate.

allowed_alternatives.proof: If each of n paths has R_i<=Rsection and genuinely joins the same bounded-access two ports, conductance sum>=n/Rsection gives effective R<=Rsection/n without equal current sharing. Add global copper/access once. The table assumes the stated number at BOTH serial sections; it is a conditional two-port construction, not the actual full multiport graph.
allowed_alternatives.scope: Use the unchanged three return wires. Preserve 4.6 A individual-wire qualification and all required outage/GH limits. All-present/two-present illustrative arithmetic is not acceptance of a failure condition; full branch loss, signed multipoint injection, shared access and GH currents still need their own compatible proof.

Rounded diagnostic only. Exact current/potential trace fields, wetted support and matching operators must be composed. Existing main-wire trial cannot be subtracted from unrelated PCB transfer intervals. It does not apply to angled CS247 contacts by common MPN alone. Source old endpoint adapter allows <=3 degree tilt to its fan; new tangent is about57 degrees from board normal and needs an explicit different/compatible termination construction.

Use existing permitted same-net layer roles, local plated transfers and retained copper; prove all pad/neck/contact fields and continuous return. Finite-conductance extraction can replace an overstrong global sum certificate with the actual joined graph, without relaxing any voltage/current limit or introducing a new interface. No asserted parallel-layer credit.

copper_and_transfer_bottleneck.array_scope: Ideal uniform annular barrels, finished bore 0.3 mm, plating 0.025 mm, 25 in parallel, rho70 nominal. Full-thickness reference comparison only; actual inner-layer transfer depths, finished thickness/etch, unequal spreading and contact fields are not resolved. Do not charge a full barrel where only a partial depth is traversed. Do not mistake this calculated value for a process maximum.
copper_and_transfer_bottleneck.design_implication: 0.1 mOhm must pay KA hub, branch/front-board access where applicable, KB spreading, every transfer/neck and matched contact observable. Two full-thickness array comparisons alone exceed it; a single broad 140 mm plane comparison exceeds it. Actual parallel surface/inner AGND may help only with proved connectivity and finite transfers; +12V, -12V and +5V have different available layer roles. No layer-role reallocation or successful copper removal is authorized.
copper_and_transfer_bottleneck.strip_scope: Explicit uniform single-plane full-width transport comparison. For a cut-free full-current slab with all injection/extraction beyond opposite ends, R>=rho*L/(t*Wmax) is a relaxation bound; no exact source/measurement slab has been established here. This is not a global impossibility proof for the actual multipoint board or parallel conductor topology. 140 mm is illustrative rounded main-land-to-feed span, not a new geometry measurement.

existing_fixture_evidence.implication: A proposal adding 12 new lands and six wires alone cannot claim complete feed/distribution; exact owned pads and returns must be joined with preserved local circuits. Historical K rail objects cannot be blindly restored by global net name.
existing_fixture_evidence.observation: The authenticated historical two-A PCB has zero tracks/vias on all four global rails and zero CS247 footprints. Five inherited filled zones do not establish all terminal paths: AGND on F/B/In1, -12 on In3, +12 on In4, no +5 zone. This is existing saved artifact evidence, not a fresh native result or inspection of a new candidate. Both boards genuinely require all four nets.

global_voltage_check.formula: 1000*(Irail*(Rmain+Rnew+Rrail_copper)+4.6*(Rmain+Rnew+Rreturn_copper)); each full wire pays both terminations once; global copper charged once. Does not assume rail cancellation, equal sharing, or reduced board planning current.
global_voltage_check.qualification: 13 mOhm/m at 70 C, 0.2 mOhm two-end allowance, 104/85 cut classes and 0.1/0.1 mOhm copper are acceptance requirements, not measurements or Alpha guarantees.

recommendation: Continue one load-side source candidate only if its first design deliverable is an exact connected rail/return/contact graph and a compatible resistance/current certificate. 104+85 mm is not rejected by the global 20 mV limit, but the 0.1/0.1 mOhm proposal is an unproved allocation with very little spare margin. Prefer explicit existing parallel-return/access modeling and physical contact matching over asserting the allocation is realizable from copied planes. No architecture adoption or physical-feasibility claim.
scope: Read-only source and lightweight arithmetic; no native, routing, placement, geometry search, hardware edit or lane edit. Upstream CN301/XB301 implementation is outside this review; preserve load-side boundary without using its non-realization to reject the requested candidate.
smallest_next_design_deliverable: One source-bound two-core load-side graph, with twelve exact implemented CS247 pad identities, contact/support geometry, every owned rail/return access, genuine stack/layer thickness bounds, and conserved load/source functionals. Compute a compatible worst-case resistance/current certificate before a physical-fit assertion. If this cannot be constructed within preserved geometry/copper, report the specific access/plane/contact deficit rather than changing limits or resuming F3 trials.

shape_and_preparation.scope: Lengths pay both bridges once and allow up to 1% C1 arclength growth of the entire new-wire path. Preparation is reserved outside that path, not available service slack. Existing main-cut qualification is an independent prerequisite; this study does not apply the new-wire shape certificate to main wires.
